params.why: the third side is then even, so PR comes out as a whole number

stem: In triangle $MNQ$, $P$ is the mid-point of $NQ$ and $R$ is the mid-point of $MQ$. One side of the triangle, $MN$, has a given length of $\frac{{=p}a}{{=d}}+{=q}$. You are now told that $PR$ has a length of ${=r}$. What is the value of $a$?
solution: $P$ is the mid-point of $NQ$ and $R$ is the mid-point of $MQ$, so $PR$ is the line joining the mid-points of two sides, and $MN$ is the third side.
From the mid-point theorem we know that the third side is twice the line joining the mid-points: $MN=2\times PR$.
notes: Modelled on ex7-7-14b (a side given in terms of a, PR given as a number, find a). The family solves by MN = 2 x PR and then a linear equation with a fraction coefficient, as the book does (the book halves the expression instead; the result is the same). The sampling picks a as a multiple of d so a is always a whole number, with gcd(p, d) = 1 so the fraction is already in lowest terms, and p*t + q even so PR is a whole number. The triangle is named in words only (P on NQ, R on MQ, third side MN) so no figure is needed.
